subject: aphid
title: This Insect Is Born Pregnant, and Its Baby Is Pregnant Too

scenes.text: Some insects are pregnant before they're even born.
Aphids, the tiny bugs on your roses, don't need males for most of the year.
A mother clones daughters inside her, and each daughter already carries her own embryo.
Three generations, nested like dolls, in one insect a few millimeters long.
One adult can give birth to about nine babies a day, so a colony can double every week.
That's why one aphid in spring becomes a plant covered in them by summer.

description:
Aphids are often born already pregnant: a female carries daughters that already have embryos of their own, a trick called telescoping generations.
For 10 to 30 generations they reproduce without males; one soybean aphid can give birth to about nine young a day, and summer colonies can double every week.
Have you ever seen a plant covered in aphids?
first_comment: Three generations inside one bug smaller than a grain of rice. Which tiny animal should we cover next?
